verification_scope_reason: Paired original Source LocalTerminalHandle(platform win32) and WindowsProcessTree compare shell/descendant activity, orphan retention, root/child PID reuse fencing, stable revision, pseudo foreground, SIGINT/TERM and refused signals. Actual current-host WinPTY tests verify C ABI resize to 73x11, TERM/session environment, Unicode output, Ctrl-C reaching a real child signal handler, process exit7/final bytes retained until cleanup, child Job termination, full output queue without consumer releasing on terminate, and real subprocess-to-controller-to-original-screen reconnect/unload. Direct legacy WinPTY, Session controller, retention/cleanup and shell discovery regressions pass.
implementation: Canonical spawnTerminal adapts the existing pre-spawn Job-owned WinPTY C ABI. A bounded async byte queue reads only available named-pipe bytes, applies backpressure, then drains the terminated pipe before closing it; final buffered bytes remain consumable. Resize RPC joins under the same native lifetime lock as writes/free. Toolhelp32/GetProcessTimes/wait-state identities fence adopted descendants; Windows shell pseudo-group and false inputWaiting match Source. SIGINT writes Ctrl-C; SIGTERM uses taskkill /T without /F; shell SIGKILL is refused. CleanupPromise moved unchanged to shared core and re-exported by retention, so the subprocess provider has no dependency on an API plugin. The raw legacy interface retains its original foreground policy.
